title: Composition of open immersions
statement:
For composable
open immersions
$U\hookrightarrow V\hookrightarrow X$, the canonical comparison

$$
(j_2)_!(j_1)_!F\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }(j_2j_1)_!F
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in $F$ and compatible with the identity
open immersion and the two ways of composing three open immersions.

proof.text: Fix the commutative coefficient ring $\Lambda$ (take $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ for abelian sheaves). Write $L_j=j_!$ and use the restriction model $R_j$ for its right adjoint, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]: for an object $a:W\to U$ of the small etale site, $(R_jG)(a)=G(j\circ a)$, with the same maps on sections and on sheaf morphisms. Write $\theta_{j,G}:j^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}R_jG$ for the cited natural identification. The adjunction with $R_j$ has Hom bijection $f\mapsto\theta_{j,G}\circ\Phi_j(f)$, where $\Phi_j$ is the cited Hom bijection for $j^{-1}$; its inverse sends $a:F\to R_jG$ to $\Phi_j^{-1}(\theta_{j,G}^{-1}\circ a)$. These maps are inverse and natural because $\Phi_j$ and $\theta_j$ are, so they specify $L_j\dashv R_j$ and its unit. On every such object and morphism, $R_{j_1}R_{j_2}G(a)=G(j_2\circ j_1\circ a)=R_{j_2j_1}G(a)$; thus these restriction models compose as equal functors. Likewise $R_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$. For three immersions all parenthesizations evaluate to $G(j_3\circ j_2\circ j_1\circ a)$ and the section maps coincide. These are statements about the chosen restriction model, not an assertion that arbitrary chosen inverse-image constructions are strictly equal. All composites in use are open immersions: by [def-weil-open-immersion] each identifies its source with an open subscheme of its target, an open subset of an open subset is open, and restricting the structure sheaf twice is restricting it once. Thus the cited adjunction applies to every composite as well as to each given immersion.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], $L_{j_2}L_{j_1}$ is left adjoint to $R_{j_1}R_{j_2}=R_{j_2j_1}$; its unit at $F$ is $R_{j_1}(\eta_{j_2,L_{j_1}F})\circ\eta_{j_1,F}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to this adjunction and $L_{j_2j_1}\dashv R_{j_2j_1}$, with the identity isomorphism of the right adjoints. It gives a unique natural isomorphism $c_{j_1,j_2}:L_{j_2}L_{j_1}\to L_{j_2j_1}$ satisfying $R_{j_2j_1}(c_{j_1,j_2,F})\circ R_{j_1}(\eta_{j_2,L_{j_1}F})\circ\eta_{j_1,F}=\eta_{j_2j_1,F}$. This is precisely the canonical comparison (the mate of the restriction identification in step 1). Its components are isomorphisms, and its naturality says $L_{j_2j_1}(b)\circ c_F=c_{F'}\circ L_{j_2}L_{j_1}(b)$ for every $b:F\to F'$. This proves both the displayed isomorphism and its naturality.

For an identity immersion write $I=L_{\mathrm{id}}$ and $\alpha:\mathrm{id}\to I$ for its unit, since $R_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$. Comparing $I\dashv\mathrm{id}$ with the identity adjunction by [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] gives an isomorphism $e:I\to\mathrm{id}$ satisfying $e_F\circ\alpha_F=\mathrm{id}_F$. Let $L=L_j$, $R=R_j$, and unit $\eta$. The composite-unit formulas of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] show that $L(e_F):LI(F)\to L(F)$ satisfies the comparison unit equation: $R(L(e_F))\circ\eta_{I(F)}\circ\alpha_F=\eta_F\circ e_F\circ\alpha_F=\eta_F$, using naturality of $\eta$. For the other order, $e_{L(F)}:IL(F)\to L(F)$ satisfies $R(e_{L(F)})\circ R(\alpha_{L(F)})\circ\eta_F=\eta_F$. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] therefore identifies $c_{\mathrm{id},j}$ with $L(e)$ and $c_{j,\mathrm{id}}$ with $e_L$. After the identity identifications these are exactly the two unit laws.

proof.text: For three immersions $X_0\hookrightarrow X_1\hookrightarrow X_2\hookrightarrow X_3$ set $\mathcal C_i=\Mod((X_i)_{\Et},\Lambda)$, let $L_{ij}$ extend by zero along the indicated composite, and let $R_{ji}$ be its restriction model from step 1. All six adjunctions exist by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. The calculation in step 1 gives exactly $R_{ki}=R_{ji}R_{kj}$ for every triple. The comparisons constructed in step 2 are exactly the unique unit-compatible $c_{ijk}$ of [lem-sc-left-adjoint-composition-iso-associativity]. That node therefore gives $c_{023,F}\circ L_{23}(c_{012,F})=c_{013,F}\circ c_{123,L_{01}F}$. The left side composes the first two immersions first and the right side the last two first, proving the required three-fold compatibility.
